title: Artin–Schreier vanishing on a smooth curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth separated connected curve
over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$.
For the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_p$, one has $H^q(C,\mathbf F_p)=0$ for $q>1$,
with cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text:
*Setup and the long exact sequence.* Let $k$ be the algebraically closed field, $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, $C$ the smooth separated connected curve [def-sc-curves], $\mathbf G_a=(\mathcal O_C)_{\mathrm{et}}$ the etale sheaf $U\mapsto\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] and $\mathbf F_p$ the constant sheaf [def-sc-constant-sheaves]. By [lem-sc-as-sequence] $0\to\mathbf F_p\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{\wp}\mathbf G_a\to0$, $\wp(x)=x^p-x$, is a short exact sequence of $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. The category $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ is Grothendieck abelian [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck], hence has enough injectives [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], and the etale cohomology $H^q(C_{\Et},-)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] (computed by K-injective resolutions) is the right derived functor $R^q\Gamma(C,-)$ of the left exact additive functor $\Gamma(C,-)$ computed by injective resolutions [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] the $R^q\Gamma(C,-)$ are additive functors and form a $\delta$-functor, so the Artin–Schreier sequence gives the exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^{q-1}(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)\xrightarrow{H^{q-1}(\wp)}H^{q-1}(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)\xrightarrow{H^q(\iota)}H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)\to\cdots\qquad(q\geq1).\qquad(*)$$

source.place: Section 0A3J (section-artin-schreier), the Artin–Schreier sequence, and Lemma 0A3N (lemma-vanishing-variety-char-p-p), proof: 'the long exact cohomology sequence associated to the Artin-Schreier sequence'

proof.text:
*Degrees $q\geq3$.* By [lem-sc-ga-cohomology] ($C$ is a smooth connected curve, $\mathbf G_a=(\mathcal O_C)_{\mathrm{et}}$) $H^j(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)\cong H^j(C,\mathcal O_C)=0$ for all $j\geq2$. For $q\geq3$ both $q-1\geq2$ and $q\geq2$, so in $(*)$ the group $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)$ sits between $H^{q-1}(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)=0$ and $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)=0$; exactness gives $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)=0$. For $q=2$ the same vanishing $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)=0$ turns $(*)$ into the exact sequence
$$H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)\xrightarrow{H^1(\wp)}H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)\to0,$$
so $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)=\operatorname{coker}H^1(\wp)$, and it remains to show that $H^1(\wp)$ is surjective.

source.place: ## Proof, proper case: 'the terms $H^q(C,\mathbf G_a)$ vanish for $q\geq2$ by [lem-sc-ga-cohomology]' and the last sentence 'for $q\geq3$ the two adjacent $\mathbf G_a$ cohomology terms vanish'; Stacks 0A3N proof, first sentence (vanishing in degrees $\geq d+2$, here $d=1$)

proof.text: *Proper or affine.* By [lem-sc-compactification] there are a proper smooth connected curve $\overline C$ over $k$ and an open immersion $C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ whose complement is a finite set of closed points. If the complement is empty, $C\cong\overline C$ is proper over $k$. Otherwise $C$ is an open subscheme of $\overline C$ with $\overline C\setminus C\neq\emptyset$, hence affine by [lem-sc-affine-open-proper].

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'By [lem-sc-compactification] and [lem-sc-affine-open-proper] the curve is either proper or affine'

proof.text: *The affine case.* If $C$ is affine, $H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)=H^1(C_{\Et},(\mathcal O_C)_{\mathrm{et}})=0$ by [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] (with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_C$). The exact sequence of step 2 then gives $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)=0$.

source.place: ## Proof: 'In the affine case, [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] gives $H^q(C,\mathbf G_a)=0$ for $q>0$, so the Artin–Schreier long exact sequence gives $H^q(C,\mathbf F_p)=0$ for $q>1$'; Stacks Lemma 0A3K (1)

proof.text: *The $k$-structure and the Frobenius on $V=H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_a)$.* For $U\to C$ in $C_{\Et}$ the ring $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is a $k$-algebra (via $U\to C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$) and the restriction maps of $\mathbf G_a$ are $k$-algebra homomorphisms. Hence for $\lambda\in k$ multiplication $m_\lambda(x)=\lambda x$ and the Frobenius $\Phi_0(x)=x^p$ are morphisms $\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_a$ in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ ($\Phi_0$ is additive because $\operatorname{char}=p$), and they satisfy $m_\lambda m_\mu=m_{\lambda\mu}$, $m_\lambda+m_\mu=m_{\lambda+\mu}$, $m_1=\mathrm{id}$, $\Phi_0m_\lambda=m_{\lambda^p}\Phi_0$ and $\wp=\Phi_0-\mathrm{id}$, all checked sectionwise. Since $H^1(C_{\Et},-)$ is an additive functor (step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor]), $\lambda\cdot v:=H^1(m_\lambda)(v)$ makes $V$ a $k$-vector space, $\Phi:=H^1(\Phi_0)$ is additive with $\Phi(\lambda v)=\lambda^p\Phi(v)$, and $H^1(\wp)=\Phi-\mathrm{id}_V$.

source.place: ## Proof, proper case: 'where $\wp=F-1$ with $F$ the $p$-linear Frobenius endomorphism of the ... $k$-vector space $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$'; Stacks 0A3N proof ('the map $F-1$ in this sequence')

proof.text: *The proper case: $V$ is finite-dimensional.* Let $C$ be proper over $k$. The structure sheaf $\mathcal O_C$ is coherent ($C$ is Noetherian) and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, so by [lem-pc-coherent-hi] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $A=k$) $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is a finite $k$-module; its $k$-module structure is the one through which $\lambda\in k$ acts by $H^1(C,m_\lambda)$, $m_\lambda$ the $\mathcal O_C$-linear multiplication by $\lambda$ on $\mathcal O_C$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. By [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison] there is an isomorphism $c^1:H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\to H^1(C_{\Et},(\mathcal O_C)_{\mathrm{et}})=V$ with $c^1\circ H^1(C,m_\lambda)=H^1(C_{\Et},(m_\lambda)_{\mathrm{et}})\circ c^1$; since $u^*\mathcal O_C=\mathcal O_U$ and $u^*(m_\lambda)$ is multiplication by $\lambda$ on $\mathcal O_U$, $(m_\lambda)_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the morphism $m_\lambda$ of step 5. So $c^1$ is $k$-linear for the structure of step 5, and $\dim_kV=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)<\infty$.

source.place: Lemma 0A3P (lemma-finiteness-proper-variety-char-p-p), proof: 'By Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02O6 and the comparison of cohomology of Theorem 03P2 the cohomology groups $H^q_\etale(X,\mathbf G_a)=H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)$ are finite dimensional $k$-vector spaces'; blueprint ## Proof: 'the finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$'

proof.text: *The proper case: conclusion.* By steps 5 and 6, $V$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p$, and $\Phi$ is $p$-linear; by [lem-sc-lang-steinberg] $\Phi-\mathrm{id}_V=H^1(\wp)$ is surjective. By the exact sequence of step 2, $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)=\operatorname{coker}H^1(\wp)=0$. Together with steps 2 and 4 (the cases are exhaustive by step 3), $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)=0$ for all $q>1$.

source.place: ## Proof: 'this cokernel is zero by [lem-sc-lang-steinberg]. Hence $H^q(C,\mathbf F_p)=0$ for $q>1$'; Stacks 0A3N proof: 'By Lemma 0A3L the map $F-1$ in this sequence is surjective'
